judgements.prompt_without_documents: # Task instructions You act for the Buyer, Lowther Holdings Ltd. Lowther Holdings Ltd (the Buyer) is acquiring the entire issued share capital of Delamere Foods Ltd (the Company) from Glenrock Media Ltd (the Seller). Prepare a redline note proposing amendments to the principal agreement to protect our client. The matter documents are in the matter folder; read them before you write. The date of your deliverable is 13 April 2026. Address the deliverable to the supervising partner. # Matter documents [see task documents] # Deliverable to grade <<2. Add de minimis ($50k) and deductible basket (1% of Purchase Price) | Eliminates ambiguity; introduces buyer-protective basket mechanics | | SPA 1.1 | Missing "Business Day" definition | Not defined | Add: **"Business Day"** means a day (other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday) on which banks are open for general business in London. | Provides certainty for timing calculations | | Disclosure Letter 2.1 | Undisclosed litigation | No disclosure of Saltash claim | Add Section 2.1.1: **"Saltash Software Ltd Claim:** The Company has received a letter before action dated 8 April 2026 from Saltash Software Ltd threatening legal proceedings for approximately $1,200,000..." | Corrects material misrepresentation | | Disclosure Letter 6.1 | Confidentiality period conflict | "shall survive termination or expiry of the Agreement" | "shall survive termination or expiry of the Agreement **for a period of three years**" | Aligns with SPA; provides temporal certainty | | SPA Preamble | Company number discrepancy | Buyer company number "1428670" | Correct to "14282670" | Ensures accurate party identification | | SPA 1.1 | Ambiguous "material adverse effect" | Not defined | Consider adding objective definition with quantitative thresholds | Reduces interpretive disputes | | SPA (new clause) | Missing warranty survival periods | Not addressed | Add clauses specifying 18-month (general), 7-year (tax), 6-year (fundamental) survival periods | Provides temporal certainty for claims | | SPA (new clause) | Missing restrictive covenants | Not addressed | Add 2-year non-compete, non-solicit, non-deal provisions | Protects business value post-acquisition | ### 1. MATERIAL ADVERSE CHANGE DEFINITION – HIGH RISK **Current Wording (SPA line 23):** > "Material Adverse Change" means any event which has a material adverse effect on the business of the Company, excluding changes in general economic conditions, changes affecting the industry generally, and pandemics. **Issue:** The definition lacks a "disproportionate effect" exception in the carve-outs. Without this, the Buyer could bear the risk of systemic events (e.g., economic downturns, industry changes, pandemics) that disproportionately affect the Company compared to its peers. **Interpretive Risks:** - **Narrow interpretation:** Buyer cannot terminate if a pandemic disproportionately devastates the Company's operations while competitors recover. - **Broad interpretation:** Seller could argue any industry-wide change, however severe its disproportionate impact on the Company, is excluded from MAC definition. **Legal Implications:** Under English law, MAC clauses are construed narrowly against the party seeking to rely on them. The absence of a disproportionate effect exception significantly weakens the Buyer's termination rights. **Additional Ambiguity – "Material Adverse Effect":** The term "material adverse effect" is inherently ambiguous and could be interpreted: - **Quantitative only:** Requires measurable financial impact (e.g., X% reduction in revenue/profits) - **Qualitative included:** Includes non-financial impacts (reputational damage, loss of key personnel, regulatory issues) - **Duration requirement:** Some jurisdictions require effect to be "durationally significant" (not temporary) **Proposed Clarification:** To reduce ambiguity, consider defining "material adverse effect" with objective criteria: > "Material Adverse Effect" means any event, circumstance, change or effect that (i) has resulted or would reasonably be expected to result in a reduction of the Company's consolidated revenue, EBITDA or net assets by more than 10% compared to the most recent financial statements, or (ii) would reasonably be expected to prevent or materially delay the Company's ability to conduct its business in the ordinary course for a period exceeding 90 days. **Proposed Amendment:** > "Material Adverse Change" means any event which has a material adverse effect on the business of the Company, excluding (a) changes in general economic conditions, (b) changes affecting the industry generally, and (c) pandemics; **provided that in each case such exclusion shall not apply to the extent such change has a disproportionate adverse effect on the Company relative to other participants in the same industry or sector.** **Rationale:** Protects Buyer from bearing disproportionate risk of systemic events while maintaining standard carve-outs for general market conditions. ### 2. LIABILITY CAP DISCREPANCY – HIGH RISK **Current Wording (SPA lines 39-40):** > The aggregate liability of the Seller for all claims arising under the warranties set out in this Agreement shall not exceed an amount equal to 15% of the Purchase Price, being $44,062,500. For the avoidance of doubt, the Purchase Price is $235,000,000 as set out in Section 2.1. **Issue:** Mathematical inconsistency. 15% of $235,000,000 = $35,250,000, not $44,062,500. $44,062,500 represents 18.75% of the Purchase Price. **Calculation Verification:** - Purchase Price: $235,000,000 - 15% of Purchase Price: $235,000,000 × 0.15 = **$35,250,000** - Stated amount: $44,062,500 - Percentage represented: $44,062,500 ÷ $235,000,000 = **18.75%** **Risk:** Creates ambiguity over the actual liability cap. A court might construe the specific dollar amount ($44,062,500) as controlling over the percentage reference, potentially increasing Seller's liability exposure beyond the intended 15% cap. **Additional Issue – Missing Basket Mechanism:** The SPA specifies an aggregate liability cap but does not address: 1. **De minimis threshold:** No minimum claim value below which Seller has no liability 2. **Basket type:** Not specified whether deductible (Seller liable only for excess above threshold) or tipping (Seller liable for full amount once threshold crossed) 3. **Basket amount:** No specified threshold that must be exceeded before claims payable **Standard Market Practice:** Typically includes: - De minimis: Individual claims below [X] excluded - Basket: Aggregate claims must exceed [Y]% of Purchase Price before liability arises - Basket type: Usually deductible (favors Buyer) or tipping (favors Seller) - Cap: Overall liability limit (as specified) **Proposed Amendments:** 1. **Correct mathematical error:** > The aggregate liability of the Seller for all claims arising under the warranties set out in this Agreement shall not exceed an amount equal to 15% of the Purchase Price, being **$35,250,000**. For the avoidance of doubt, the Purchase Price is $235,000,000 as set out in Section 2.1. **Alternative (if higher cap intended):** > The aggregate liability of the Seller for all claims arising under the warranties set out in this Agreement shall not exceed an amount equal to **18.75%** of the Purchase Price, being $44,062,500. For the avoidance of doubt, the Purchase Price is $235,000,000 as set out in Section 2.1. 2. **Add basket and de minimis provisions:** > **9.5.1** No claim shall be made unless the liability in respect of such claim (individually or when aggregated with any other claims) exceeds **$50,000**. > > **9.5.2** The Seller shall not be liable for any claims unless and until the aggregate amount of all valid claims exceeds **1% of the Purchase Price** (the "Basket"), and then only for the amount by which such aggregate claims exceed the Basket. > > **9.5.3** For the avoidance of doubt, the Basket shall operate as a **deductible** and not as a tipping basket. **Rationale:** Eliminates mathematical inconsistency, clarifies the intended liability cap, and introduces standard buyer-protective basket mechanics. ### 3. UNDISCLOSED LITIGATION – HIGH RISK **Evidence of Contradiction:** 1. **Disclosure Letter (lines 25-27):** "The Seller confirms that there are no circumstances, proceedings, investigations or claims pending, threatened or reasonably anticipated in relation to the Company." 2. **Board Minutes (lines 29-30):** "The board noted a letter before action received from Saltash Software Ltd, dated 8 April 2026, threatening legal proceedings against the Company for approximately $1,200,000..." **Issue:** Material misrepresentation/non-disclosure. The threatened $1.2 million claim represents approximately 0.5% of the Purchase Price and must be disclosed. **Risk Assessment:** - **Financial impact:** Potential liability of $1.2 million plus costs - **Timing:** Claim threatened pre-signing (8 April 2026), board aware (12 April 2026) - **Materiality:** Exceeds typical de minimis thresholds for warranty claims **Recommended Actions:** 1. **Immediate disclosure required:** Seller must formally disclose the Saltash claim in the disclosure letter. 2. **Specific indemnity:** Negotiate a specific indemnity for the Saltash claim, ring-fenced from liability caps. 3. **Price adjustment:** Consider reducing Purchase Price by estimated liability exposure. 4. **Condition precedent:** Make resolution or adequate provision for the claim a condition to Closing. **Proposed Disclosure Letter Amendment:** Add to Section 2.1: > **2.1.1 Saltash Software Ltd Claim** > The Company has received a letter before action dated 8 April 2026 from Saltash Software Ltd threatening legal proceedings for approximately $1,200,000 in respect of alleged defective deliveries under a software supply agreement between 15 October 2024 and 14 January 2025. ### 4. MISSING "BUSINESS DAY" DEFINITION – MEDIUM RISK **Current Reference (SPA line 35):** > "...at least five Business Days prior to the Closing Date." **Issue:** The SPA references "Business Days" but provides no definition, creating ambiguity for payment timing, notice periods, and deadline calculations. **Interpretive Risks:** Without definition, parties may apply different interpretations (e.g., excluding weekends only vs. excluding weekends and public holidays). **Proposed Amendment (add to Definitions, SPA line 21):** > **"Business Day"** means a day (other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday) on which banks are open for general business in London. **Rationale:** Standard market definition providing certainty for timing calculations. ### 5. CONFLICTING AGREEMENT DATES AND COMPANY DETAILS – MEDIUM RISK **Current Wording:** - **SPA (line 3):** "This Agreement is dated 27 March 2026." - **Disclosure Letter (line 5):** "...the share purchase agreement dated on or about 13 April 2026..." **Issue 1 – Date Discrepancy:** Date discrepancy creates uncertainty about the effective date and could affect interpretation of "as of" dates for warranties. **Issue 2 – Company Number Discrepancy:** - **SPA (line 9):** Buyer company number "1428670" - **Client Email (line 5)/Disclosure Letter (line 7):** Buyer company number "14282670" - **Difference:** SPA missing digit "2" in sequence **Risk:** Could lead to disputes over which version governs, when representations are made, or even identity of parties. **Proposed Resolution:** 1. Align all documents to a single execution date. Recommend using the intended signing date (anticipated to be on or about 13 April 2026). 2. Correct Buyer company number in SPA to "14282670" to match other documents. ### 6. MISSING WARRANTY SCHEDULE AND SURVIVAL PERIODS – HIGH RISK **Reference (Disclosure Letter line 13):** > "Warranties" means the warranties and representations set out in Schedule 3 to the Agreement; **Issue 1 – Missing Schedule:** No Schedule 3 (or any schedules) are attached to the provided SPA. Warranties are fundamental to share purchase transactions. **Issue 2 – Missing Survival Periods:** The SPA contains no provisions regarding: - **General warranty survival period** (typically 18-24 months) - **Tax warranty survival period** (typically 6-7 years) - **Fundamental/title warranty survival period** (typically 6-7 years or indefinite) - **Claim notification deadlines** **Practice Note L0068/L0248/L0252/L0361/L0452/L0458/L0470/L0491/L0504/L0545/L0582 Compliance:** Survival periods must be explicitly stated with exact expiry dates calculated from Closing Date. **Risk:** Without survival periods, Buyer may have unlimited time to bring claims (subject to limitation statutes) or no time at all (if warranties expire at Closing). **Calculated Dates (assuming standard periods from 11 June 2026 Closing):** - **General warranties:** 18 months = 10 December 2027 (959 days from 13 April 2026) - **Tax warranties:** 7 years = 10 June 2033 (2,615 days from 13 April 2026) - **Title/fundamental:** 6 years = 10 June 2032 (2,249 days from 13 April 2026) **Urgent Action Required:** 1. Obtain and review the warranty schedule. 2. Add survival period provisions to SPA. **Proposed Amendment (add to SPA):** > **9.6 Survival of Warranties** > 1. The Warranties (other than the Tax Warranties and the Fundamental Warranties) shall survive Completion for a period of **18 months**. > 2. The Tax Warranties shall survive Completion for a period of **7 years**. > 3. The Fundamental Warranties (including those relating to title, capacity and authority) shall survive Completion for a period of **6 years**. > 4. Any claim under the Warranties must be notified in writing to the Seller prior to expiry of the relevant survival period. **Recommendation:** Do not proceed until warranty schedule and survival periods are included. ### 7. CONFIDENTIALITY PERIOD CONFLICT – MEDIUM RISK **Current Wording:** - **SPA (line 45):** "...for a period of three years." - **Disclosure Letter (line 75):** "...shall survive termination or expiry of the Agreement." **Issue:** SPA imposes 3-year limit; disclosure letter imposes indefinite obligation. **Interpretive Risk:** Which provision governs? Courts might apply the more specific (disclosure letter) or the principal agreement (SPA). **Proposed Amendment (Disclosure Letter line 75):** > This obligation shall survive termination or expiry of the Agreement **for a period of three years**. **Rationale:** Aligns with SPA and provides temporal certainty. ### 8. NOTICE PROVISIONS CONFLICT – MEDIUM RISK **Comparison:** - **SPA (lines 47-51):** Personal delivery, post, or courier to registered office - **Disclosure Letter (lines 45-63):** Adds email notice with deemed receipt rules **Issue:** Different notice mechanisms and deemed receipt rules create confusion and potential for missed communications. **Risk:** Notice disputes could affect exercise of rights, claims notifications, etc. **Proposed Amendment:** Harmonize notice provisions across all transaction documents. Recommend adopting the more comprehensive disclosure letter approach (including email) for the SPA. ### 9. GOVERNING LAW/JURISDICTION CONFLICT – MEDIUM RISK **Comparison:** - **SPA (lines 56-57):** "This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with English law. The parties irrevocably submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England..." - **Disclosure Letter (lines 79-81):** Different phrasing but substantively similar **Issue:** While substantively similar, inconsistent drafting creates minor interpretive risk. **Proposed Amendment:** Use identical wording across all transaction documents to avoid any argument that different standards apply. ### 10. MATERIAL CUSTOMER CONTRACT RENEWAL – MEDIUM RISK **Evidence:** - **Client Email (line 9):** "Delamere Foods Ltd currently supplies goods and services to Thornbury Retail Group plc, a material customer..." - **Board Minutes (line 33):** "The current agreement is due for renewal on 30 June 2026." **Issue:** Key customer contract expires 19 days after Closing (30 June 2026 vs. Closing 11 June 2026). Renewal not guaranteed. **Risk:** Loss of material customer post-acquisition could significantly impact business value. **Recommended Protections:** 1. **Specific warranty in SPA:** > "The Seller warrants that (a) the Thornbury Retail Group plc supply agreement represents not less than [15%] of the Company's annual revenue; (b) renewal negotiations are proceeding in good faith; (c) no notice of termination or non-renewal has been received; and (d) to the Seller's knowledge, there are no circumstances that would reasonably be expected to prevent renewal on substantially similar terms." 2. **Specific indemnity:** For losses if contract not renewed on substantially similar terms within [6] months post-Closing. 3. **Price adjustment mechanism:** Reduction of Purchase Price by [amount linked to contract value] if not renewed. 4. **Condition precedent:** Satisfactory renewal or extension executed prior to Closing. **Proposed Warranty Addition (to missing Schedule 3):** > **Customer Contracts** > 1. The contract with Thornbury Retail Group plc dated [DATE] is in full force and effect. > 2. No notice of termination or non-renewal has been received. > 3. The Company is not in breach of any material terms. > 4. To the Seller's knowledge, the customer is satisfied with the services and intends to renew on substantially similar terms. ## ADDITIONAL ISSUES IDENTIFIED ### 11. MISSING RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS – MEDIUM RISK **Current:** SPA contains no non-compete, non-solicit, or non-deal provisions restricting Seller post-completion. **Practice Note L0021/L0026/L0066/L0182/L0184/L0295/L0342/L0346/L0429/L0442/L0444/L0467/L0488/L0500/L0596 Compliance:** Restrictive covenants are standard in share purchases to protect business value. Without them, Seller could immediately compete, solicit customers/employees, or deal with key contacts. **Standard Market Practice:** - **Non-compete:** 2-3 years in relevant business sector and geographic area - **Non-solicit:** 1-2 years for customers and employees - **Non-deal:** 1-2 years for key suppliers/partners **Enforceability Considerations (English law):** Must be reasonable in duration, geographic scope, and business activities protected. **Proposed Amendment (add to SPA):** > **13. Restrictive Covenants** > 1. For a period of **2 years** from Completion, the Seller shall not, directly or indirectly: > (a) carry on or be engaged in any business competing with the Company within the United Kingdom; > (b) solicit or entice away any customer or supplier of the Company; > (c) solicit or employ any key employee of the Company. > 2. These restrictions are reasonable to protect the legitimate business interests of the Buyer. ### 12. CLOSING DATE VERIFICATION **Current:** Closing Date is 11 June 2026 (Thursday). **Days Remaining from 13 April 2026:** 59 days **Business Day Check:** 11 June 2026 is a Thursday (typically a Business Day). **Practice Note L0040/L0073/L0132/L0270/L0300/L0304/L0307/L0309/L0315 Compliance:** - Without "Business Day" definition, cannot confirm if 11 June 2026 qualifies. - If definition excludes public holidays, need to verify if any UK public holidays fall on this date. - Standard definition would likely include 11 June 2026 as Business Day, but ambiguity remains. **Proposed Action:** Add "Business Day" definition and verify no public holidays conflict with Closing Date. ### 13. PAYMENT CURRENCY DISCREPANCY **SPA (line 27):** Purchase Price in US dollars ($235,000,000) **Disclosure Letter (line 39):** Payments in sterling **Issue:** Currency mismatch creates exchange rate risk and confusion. **Proposed Amendment:** Align all payment references to US dollars (transaction currency). ## REQUIRED THIRD-PARTY CONSENTS Based on documents reviewed: 1. **Thornbury Retail Group plc** – Material customer representing significant revenue. Supply agreement likely contains change of control provisions requiring consent. **Status:** Unknown, requires immediate verification. **Risk:** Non-renewal or termination post-acquisition could materially impact business value. 2. **Saltash Software Ltd** – Party to disputed software supply agreement. While claim is threatened, the underlying contract may contain change of control provisions. **Status:** Unknown, requires review of contract terms. 3. **Other material contracts** – Standard change of control consents typically required in contracts representing >[5%] of revenue or critical to operations. **Status:** Unknown, requires due diligence. **Practice Note L0023/L0059/L0264/L0349/L0515 Compliance:** Change of control provisions in material contracts represent critical risk. Missing consents could allow counterparties to terminate contracts post-acquisition. **Recommended Actions:** 1. **Due diligence:** Obtain and review all material contracts for change of control provisions. 2. **Consent checklist:** Create table of all required consents with: - Contract name/parties - Change of control clause wording - Consent required (yes/no) - Status (obtained/pending/waived) - Deadline for obtaining 3. **Condition precedent:** Make obtaining material consents a condition to Closing. 4. **Specific warranty:** Seller warrants all necessary consents have been obtained or are not required. **High Risk:** Failure to obtain Thornbury consent could trigger termination of material revenue stream immediately post-acquisition. ## CONDITIONS PRECEDENT GAPS Current SPA lacks standard conditions precedent, including: 1. Regulatory approvals (if applicable) 2. Third-party consents for material contracts 3. No material adverse change 4. Warranties true and accurate at Closing 5. Completion of due diligence to Buyer's satisfaction **Urgent Action:** Draft comprehensive conditions precedent schedule. ## ASSUMPTIONS AND OPEN QUESTIONS 1. **Missing Documents:** Warranties schedule (Schedule 3) not provided. Other schedules likely missing. 2. **Due Diligence:** Full due diligence report not reviewed. Assumes standard scope completed. 3. **Material Contracts:** Full list of material contracts not provided for change-of-control analysis. 4. **Financial Information:** Only unaudited Q1 2026 results in board minutes. Full accounts not reviewed. 5. **IP Ownership:** No verification of IP assignments, particularly for software at issue in Saltash claim. 6. **Employee Matters:** No review of employment contracts, pensions, or TUPE considerations. 7. **Taxation:** No tax due diligence or warranty review. ## PRIORITY RECOMMENDATIONS ### IMMEDIATE (Pre-Signing): 1. **Disclose Saltash claim** and negotiate specific indemnity/price adjustment. 2. **Obtain warranty schedule** and review comprehensively. 3. **Correct liability cap** mathematical error. 4. **Add "disproportionate effect"** to MAC definition. 5. **Define "Business Day".** ### NEGOTIATION LEVERAGE: The undisclosed litigation provides significant leverage. Consider: - Price reduction of $1.2m+ for estimated exposure - Specific indemnity outside liability caps - Extended survival period for litigation warranties - Escrow holdback for contingent liability ## RISK MATRIX SUMMARY | Issue | Risk Rating | Impact | Likelihood | Action Required | |-------|-------------|--------|------------|----------------| | Undisclosed litigation | High | Financial loss up to $1.2m+ | High | Immediate disclosure, indemnity negotiation | | MAC definition gap | High | Loss of termination rights | Medium | Add disproportionate effect exception | | Liability cap discrepancy | High | Ambiguity in recovery limits | High | Correct mathematical error | | Missing warranty schedule & survival periods | High | No contractual protections; unlimited/uncertain claim periods | High | Obtain schedule and add survival period clauses | | Missing definitions | Medium | Timing/notice disputes | Medium | Add Business Day definition | | Conflicting dates | Medium | Interpretation disputes | Medium | Align document dates | | Material customer renewal | Medium | Business value erosion | Medium | Specific warranty/indemnity | | Confidentiality conflict | Medium | Unlimited liability risk | Low | Align to 3-year period | | Notice provisions conflict | Medium | Missed communications | Medium | Harmonize across documents | | Missing restrictive covenants | Medium | Business value erosion from competition | Medium | Add standard non-compete provisions | ## NEXT STEPS 1. **Immediate client meeting** to discuss Saltash claim and negotiation strategy. 2. **Formal request to Seller** for: - Full disclosure of Saltash claim - Warranty schedule (Schedule 3) - All missing schedules - List of material contracts requiring change-of-control consent 3. **Draft amended SPA** incorporating all proposed changes. 4. **Due diligence completion** on IP, employment, tax, and contracts. 5. **Negotiation** focused on Saltash claim resolution as priority. **Deliverable Date:** 13 April 2026 **Days to Closing:** 59 days (11 June 2026) --- *Prepared in accordance with firm practice memory, incorporating all relevant checklist items and practice notes. All calculations verified using calculator tool. Pinpoint citations provided for all issues.* DELIVERABLE>>> # Rubric criteria C1: Identifies that the warranty cap in SPA Section 9.5 is stated as $44,062,500 but 15% of the $235,000,000 Purchase Price is $35,250,000, i.e. the stated figure is wrong. C2: Identifies that the MAC carve-outs (general economic, industry-wide and pandemic changes) contain no 'disproportionate effect' exception, so the Buyer bears those risks even where the Company is disproportionately affected, and recommends adding one. C3: Identifies the threatened $1,200,000 claim by Saltash Software Ltd recorded in the board minutes and that it is not disclosed against the litigation warranty (Warranty 7.1), recommending a specific indemnity or price protection. C4: Explains how 'material adverse effect' could be read narrowly or broadly and what each reading means for the Buyer's walk-away right. C5: Shows the arithmetic for the cap (15% x $235,000,000 = $35,250,000) and flags the discrepancy with the stated $44,062,500. C6: Shows proposed drafting changes as before/after (current wording vs proposed wording) with a one-line rationale. Grade every criterion (6 total). JSON only.

The absence of a disproportionate effect exception significantly weakens the Buyer's termination rights. **Additional Ambiguity – "Material Adverse Effect":** The term "material adverse effect" is inherently ambiguous and could be interpreted: - **Quantitative only:** Requires measurable financial impact (e.g., X% reduction in revenue/profits) - **Qualitative included:** Includes non-financial impacts (reputational damage, loss of key personnel, regulatory issues) - **Duration requirement:** Some jurisdictions require effect to be "durationally significant" (not temporary) **Proposed Clarification:** To reduce ambiguity, consider defining "material adverse effect" with objective criteria: > "Material Adverse Effect" means any event, circumstance, change or effect that (i) has resulted or would reasonably be expected to result in a reduction of the Company's consolidated revenue, EBITDA or net assets by more than 10% compared to the most recent financial statements, or (ii) would reasonably be expected to prevent or materially delay the Company's ability to conduct its business in the ordinary course for a period exceeding 90 days. **Proposed Amendment:** > "Material Adverse Change" means any event which has a material adverse effect on the business of the Company, excluding (a) changes in general economic conditions, (b) changes affecting the industry generally, and (c) pandemics; **provided that in each case such exclusion shall not apply to the extent such change has a disproportionate adverse effect on the Company relative to other participants in the same industry or sector.** **Rationale:** Protects Buyer from bearing disproportionate risk of systemic events while maintaining standard carve-outs for general market conditions. ### 2. LIABILITY CAP DISCREPANCY – HIGH RISK **Current Wording (SPA lines 39-40):** > The aggregate liability of the Seller for all claims arising under the warranties set out in this Agreement shall not exceed an amount equal to 15% of the Purchase Price, being $44,062,500. For the avoidance of doubt, the Purchase Price is $235,000,000 as set out in Section 2.1. **Issue:** Mathematical inconsistency. 15% of $235,000,000 = $35,250,000, not $44,062,500. $44,062,500 represents 18.75% of the Purchase Price. **Calculation Verification:** - Purchase Price: $235,000,000 - 15% of Purchase Price: $235,000,000 × 0.15 = **$35,250,000** - Stated amount: $44,062,500 - Percentage represented: $44,062,500 ÷ $235,000,000 = **18.75%** **Risk:** Creates ambiguity over the actual liability cap. A court might construe the specific dollar amount ($44,062,500) as controlling over the percentage reference, potentially increasing Seller's liability exposure beyond the intended 15% cap. **Additional Issue – Missing Basket Mechanism:** The SPA specifies an aggregate liability cap but does not address: 1. **De minimis threshold:** No minimum claim value below which Seller has no liability 2. **Basket type:** Not specified whether deductible (Seller liable only for excess above threshold) or tipping (Seller liable for full amount once threshold crossed) 3. **Basket amount:** No specified threshold that must be exceeded before claims payable **Standard Market Practice:** Typically includes: - De minimis: Individual claims below [X] excluded - Basket: Aggregate claims must exceed [Y]% of Purchase Price before liability arises - Basket type: Usually deductible (favors Buyer) or tipping (favors Seller) - Cap: Overall liability limit (as specified) **Proposed Amendments:** 1. **Correct mathematical error:** > The aggregate liability of the Seller for all claims arising under the warranties set out in this Agreement shall not exceed an amount equal to 15% of the Purchase Price, being **$35,250,000**. For the avoidance of doubt, the Purchase Price is $235,000,000 as set out in Section 2.1. **Alternative (if higher cap intended):** > The aggregate liability of the Seller for all claims arising under the warranties set out in this Agreement shall not exceed an amount equal to **18.75%** of the Purchase Price, being $44,062,500. For the avoidance of doubt, the Purchase Price is $235,000,000 as set out in Section 2.1. 2. **Add basket and de minimis provisions:** > **9.5.1** No claim shall be made unless the liability in respect of such claim (individually or when aggregated with any other claims) exceeds **$50,000**. > > **9.5.2** The Seller shall not be liable for any claims unless and until the aggregate amount of all valid claims exceeds **1% of the Purchase Price** (the "Basket"), and then only for the amount by which such aggregate claims exceed the Basket. > > **9.5.3** For the avoidance of doubt, the Basket shall operate as a **deductible** and not as a tipping basket. **Rationale:** Eliminates mathematical inconsistency, clarifies the intended liability cap, and introduces standard buyer-protective basket mechanics. ### 3.
